title: Calculus of Robinet: completely positive reconstruction of time-averaged diffusive quantum trajectories
abstract: Truly continuous quantum trajectories, obtained from homodyne or heterodyne readouts, can only ever be reconstructed approximately. The continuous measurement signal, needed for exact reconstruction, is averaged over bins of finite time $Δt$ during any analog to digital conversion step. The best reconstruction possible, knowing only this discrete record, was introduced recently and dubbed the Robinet state. In this article, we show how the Robinet state can be computed with a numerical discretization scheme that is completely positive, accurate to arbitrarily high order in $Δt$, and that does not rely on any other external solver. Our derivation relies on a dilation of the stochastic master equation into a system + transmission line setup, constructed in such a way that measuring what we call the "zero mode" of the line yields the Robinet state. We test the method on a challenging example with random Hamiltonian and jump operator, and verify its accuracy up to order $10$. Apart from its numerical interest, our approach provides a wealth of physical insights, extending in particular recent results on purity obtained by Wonglakhon, Chantasri, and Wiseman, that would be difficult to obtain in any other way.
summary: This paper tackles the challenge of reconstructing true quantum states from digitized measurement data by defining and calculating the 'Robinet state'. The authors introduce a novel mathematical technique based on unitary dilation that yields an exactly completely positive evolution map, allowing for highly accurate simulation of time-averaged quantum trajectories.
main_problem: The core problem is accurately reconstructing quantum states from continuous measurement records that are inherently digitized, leading to information loss due to finite time binning ($\Delta t$).
main_result: The authors developed a novel numerical discretization scheme for the 'Robinet state' reconstruction map that is provably completely positive and accurate to arbitrarily high orders in $\Delta t$ without needing external solvers.
method: The method involves constructing an explicit, completely positive evolution map by employing a unitary dilation of the stochastic master equation into an augmented system plus transmission line setup.
model_or_system: The model describes a finite-dimensional quantum system undergoing open evolution governed by a Hamiltonian $H$ and measured via an operator $L$. The dynamics are analyzed using the Stochastic Master Equation (SME) framework.
key_observables: The Robinet state ($ ar{ho}_n$), which is the time-averaged density matrix conditioned on the discrete measurement record $\{I_k\}$.
important_parameters: The time bin size $\Delta t$, and the measurement efficiency $\eta$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on extending the stochastic master equation via a unitary dilation, which is systematic but involves truncating infinite series for practical computation.
figures_summary: No explicit figure summaries are available; the notes indicate extensive mathematical derivations and tabulated coefficients related to time-step expansions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the information loss problem (Robinet state) to introducing the unitary dilation formalism. It then details deriving the completely positive map $K_{In}$ through this dilation, verifying its accuracy on challenging examples, and finally providing physical insights by comparing results with prior work.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant for theoretical physicists working on open quantum systems or quantum optics, as it provides a rigorous, computationally tractable method to handle the non-Markovian effects inherent in real-world continuous quantum measurements.
